chunks: And from him from Ayoub ibn Nuh al-Nakha'i from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ali ibn Yaqtin from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujood): how many glorifications (tasbih) are sufficient in them? He said, 'Three, and one is sufficient for you if you can place your forehead on the ground.'
ai.seo_question: How many times should one recite tasbih during ruku and sujud in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the flexibility in the number of glorifications (tasbih) recited during bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujood). He establishes that while three repetitions are the standard sufficiency, a single recitation is also valid provided the worshipper can fully lower their forehead to the ground, emphasizing the link between physical humility and spiritual devotion. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease in worship when physical conditions allow for greater devotion.
